extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers (literary and genre), especially those writing suspense/genre and prompt-driven short fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing fiction that 'thrills'—prioritizing urgency, momentum, and reader attention by borrowing techniques from genre and screenwriting. Emphasizes page-level propulsion, restrained backstory, cinematic modulation, and earned violence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Urgency Above All
rubrics_metrics.description: Every page must propel forward; if the reader can put the book down without curiosity to continue, you've failed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure there is forward momentum on every page — questions, stakes, or tension that compel reading. Test: 'Does the reader want to keep going?' and 'Is there urgency on every page?'

rubrics_metrics.name: Thrill the Reader (Propel the Story)
rubrics_metrics.description: The central mandate: 'Thrill the reader' by creating momentum, suspense, and continual curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plot, suspense, and momentum strategically so the story continually raises queries or stakes. Percy argues this is as important in literary fiction as in genre fiction and may predict reader engagement (e.g., upvotes in prompt-driven contexts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lessons from Pop Genre Masters
rubrics_metrics.description: Refuse the literary/commercial hierarchy and learn from SF, fantasy, mystery, horror and pop-genre exemplars (Percy quotes works like Jaws, Blood Meridian, The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study how genre masters create suspense, pacing, and emotional engagement; borrow mechanics and storytelling habits regardless of perceived literary status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cinematic Modulation / Filmmaking Lessons
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply screenwriting techniques to fiction: hard cuts between scenes, visual storytelling, rule-of-three setups, cliffhanger chapter endings, match-cuts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think in visual beats and cutting points; end chapters on cliffhangers; use match-cuts and hard scene transitions to maintain momentum. Percy leverages his screenwriting experience to argue these techniques translate to page-driven suspense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backstory: Less Is More
rubrics_metrics.description: Backstory belongs in the writer's head, not on the page; avoid 'backstory-dumps.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When backstory must appear, make it brief, triggered by present action, carry emotional weight, and appear in dialogue or action rather than expository narration. Ensure backstory is earned and essential to current stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violence Done Right
rubrics_metrics.description: Violence must be earned, specific, and consequential — not generic blood-and-guts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use violence to reveal character and consequences. Avoid gratuitous or vague depictions; make violent acts meaningful within the story's moral and emotional architecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modulation Between Scene and Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Consciously shift between scene (in-the-moment dramatization) and summary (narrative compression) to control pace and focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose scene for moments of tension and emotional detail; use summary to move quickly through lower-stakes time. Modulate length and intensity to keep forward momentum without exhausting the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Vary scene length; use chapter endings as cliffhangers; cut at the moment of maximum tension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate long and short scenes to create rhythm. End scenes/chapters when tension peaks to compel the next turn of the page. Reassess scene length to sustain urgency and avoid lulls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character, Setting, Dialogue (as tools of propulsion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Character, setting, and dialogue are core topics for generating interest, conflict, and movement in fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use character choices, evocative setting, and dialogue that reveals information and pushes scenes forward. Ensure these elements contribute to urgency rather than stalling the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Tests / Checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of quick tests to evaluate whether work meets Percy's standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask: 'Does the reader want to keep going?'; 'Is there urgency on every page?'; 'Is backstory minimal and earned?'; 'Does the prose move?'; 'Are scenes ended at the right moment?'; 'Does this story care about the reader's experience?' Use these to judge drafts and guide revisions.
